title: THE WORLD'S RICHEST INVESTORS USE THESE TINY ISLANDS. HERE'S WHY

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your retirement money could be passing through a tiny island in the Caribbean right now.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You've probably never been there. You might not even know where it is on a map.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But some of the world's largest investment funds are legally registered there. Funds connected to wealthy investors, major financial institutions, and retirement savings.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And here's the strange part.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The money doesn't necessarily stay on the island.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It might never physically go there at all.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: So why would an investment company in New York set up a fund thousands of miles away, in a place with beautiful beaches, a small population, and no major stock exchange?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Why would investors from London, Tokyo, and other financial capitals use a company registered on a Caribbean island to invest in businesses somewhere else?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And why have so many of them made that choice?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: By the third quarter of 2026, more than 31,500 regulated investment funds were registered in the Cayman Islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Thirty-one thousand, five hundred.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: On three small islands in the Caribbean Sea.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These aren't all small private accounts belonging to people trying to hide money. They're investment fund structures used in a global industry that connects institutions, businesses, and investors across borders.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some of these arrangements serve ordinary, lawful financial purposes. Others have been used in ways that raise serious questions about taxes, secrecy, and who really benefits.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the deeper you follow the money, the stranger the picture becomes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because the biggest financial centers aren't always the places where money is earned.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Sometimes, they're the places where the legal documents say an investment belongs.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That difference matters more than most people realize.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If your retirement savings were invested through a fund registered thousands of miles away, would that bother you? Or would you care more about whether the investment was properly regulated, adequately protected, and performing well?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: I'd be interested to know which matters more to you.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because by the end of this documentary, you'll understand why that question is harder to answer than it first appears.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We're going to follow one investment from its original owner, through a small Caribbean territory, and into the businesses where the capital is actually put to work.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We'll see how these islands became important to global finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We'll examine who earns money from the arrangement.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And we'll look at the problems that have made offshore finance one of the most controversial parts of the modern economy.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But first, there's a number that makes the entire story difficult to ignore.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In March 2026, the Bank for International Settlements published research on a group of cross-border financial centers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These included small jurisdictions such as Bermuda and the Cayman Islands, along with other places specializing in financial business involving nonresidents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The researchers found that by 2023, these centers accounted for almost sixty trillion dollars in external financial positions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Nearly thirty percent of the worldwide total.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Yet the economies of those same centers represented just 2.8 percent of global economic activity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now, that sixty trillion dollars is not a pile of cash hidden beneath tropical islands. It represents financial assets and liabilities recorded across a broader group of financial centers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the contrast tells us something extraordinary.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A relatively small part of the world's real economy has become a major part of the international financial system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: How did that happen?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: To find the answer, we're going to a place that, not so long ago, had almost none of the things you would expect from a financial powerhouse.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Geography: The Three Islands

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Look at the western Caribbean.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: South of Cuba and northwest of Jamaica, you'll find three islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac, and Little Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Together, they form the Cayman Islands, a British Overseas Territory.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They are not a sovereign country. They have their own domestic institutions and a substantial degree of self-government, while retaining constitutional ties to the United Kingdom.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Today, the territory is known for tourism, international business, and financial services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But that wasn't always the case.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For much of its history, Cayman was a small maritime community.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: People made their living through fishing, seafaring, trade, and work connected to the wider Caribbean.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There was no enormous manufacturing industry.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: No vast domestic market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: No major stock exchange attracting companies from every continent.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And unlike some countries that became wealthy by exploiting valuable natural resources, Cayman had no giant oil industry waiting to be developed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Even ordinary banking arrived relatively late.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: According to the Cayman Islands Government's historical records, the first commercial bank opened in 1953.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Barclays established a presence in George Town, the territory's main commercial center.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Think about what that means.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In the early 1950s, when New York and London had already spent generations building powerful banking institutions, Cayman was only beginning to develop the commercial banking services that people in those cities took for granted.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There was nothing inevitable about what happened next.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In 1970, Cayman's recorded population was only 10,249.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A place that small could not compete with the United States through domestic consumer spending.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It could not match Germany through industrial production.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it wasn't going to become another London simply by building taller office blocks.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But while Cayman's domestic economy was small, the international financial system was changing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And those changes created an opportunity that had little to do with population size.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: After the Second World War, international commerce expanded.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Multinational companies became more important.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Banks developed relationships that reached across national borders.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Investors increasingly wanted access to opportunities in other countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the movement of capital became more complicated than the old picture of money being deposited in one local bank and lent to a nearby business.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Large financial institutions were moving money, creating credit, and organizing investments across several legal systems at once.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One important development involved international dollar banking.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: US dollars were increasingly being deposited, borrowed, and lent through financial institutions outside the United States.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This became known as the Eurodollar market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Despite its name, the Eurodollar market had nothing to do with the modern euro currency.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It referred to dollar-denominated banking activity outside the American domestic banking system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: London became especially important in that market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the broader growth of international finance opened opportunities for other jurisdictions too.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Banks and investors needed places where companies could be established, transactions could be documented, and international business could operate under predictable rules.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And this is where Cayman's story takes an unexpected turn.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its leaders and financial professionals began building an industry around something that couldn't be mined, shipped, or manufactured.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They built it around law.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In the 1960s, Cayman introduced legislation that helped attract international banking and trust businesses.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One important milestone came in 1966, when new legislation was introduced to encourage the banking industry.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Company law, trust arrangements, and professional services developed alongside these changes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The territory gradually became a place where international businesses could establish legal entities and organize financial affairs under a familiar legal framework.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This didn't turn every resident into a millionaire.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it didn't happen overnight.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it gave Cayman something valuable to offer a growing international market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A jurisdiction in which financial businesses could establish companies, organize contractual relationships, and obtain specialized professional services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There was another attraction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman did not impose the kind of ordinary direct income taxes found in many larger economies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That mattered to international investors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it wasn't the entire reason.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If low taxes alone created successful financial centers, every jurisdiction with low taxes would become a global financial powerhouse.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That hasn't happened.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Investors also care about whether contracts can be enforced.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They care about company law.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They care about access to legal professionals, administrators, accountants, banks, and regulators.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And they care about knowing what will happen if a dispute arises or an investment goes wrong.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An attractive tax system doesn't help much if investors don't trust the institutions surrounding it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman gradually developed a combination of financial services, legal structures, and specialist expertise that international businesses were prepared to use.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: By the time global investment funds became a much larger industry, Cayman already had part of the necessary infrastructure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That turned out to be extremely important.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because the biggest opportunity wasn't simply opening more local bank accounts.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It was helping investors organize financial relationships that stretched across the world.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: How Offshore Finance Works

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine you own a business.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its headquarters are in London.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its customers are in America.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its factories are in Vietnam.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its software engineers work in India.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And its shareholders live in several countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Where is the business?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There isn't one answer that describes everything it does.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its headquarters have a location.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its factories have locations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its employees have locations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the legal entities that own different parts of the business may be incorporated in different countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Modern international finance takes this separation even further.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A financial company can be legally registered in the Cayman Islands while the people making its investment decisions work in New York.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its investors may live in Europe, Asia, and North America.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The securities it holds may be issued by businesses operating on several continents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its administrator, custodian, and bankers may be located in still more places.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal registration tells us something important about the entity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it doesn't tell us the location of every person, account, or asset connected to it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is the first thing you need to understand about offshore finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A fund can be registered in a country without all its money being deposited there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And a company can be incorporated in a jurisdiction without carrying out most of its commercial activity inside that territory.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't make the company imaginary.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal entity is real.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its contracts matter.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its investors have rights.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its managers and directors have responsibilities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its governing law can affect how disputes are resolved.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And its regulatory status can determine which requirements apply to its operation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the legal location is only one part of the financial arrangement.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Consider a simple example.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An investment fund wants to raise money from several institutional investors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One investor is a pension fund in Canada.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Another is an endowment in Europe.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A third is an investment institution based in Asia.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund intends to invest in companies around the world.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It needs a legal vehicle through which these investors can participate.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It also needs rules.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who can invest?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who makes the decisions?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What happens if an investor wants to withdraw?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: How are returns divided?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who pays the investment manager?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What happens if the fund loses money?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And whose law governs the agreements?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Those questions matter just as much as the physical location of the money.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund's organizers could choose from several different jurisdictions, depending on the investors, strategy, and applicable laws.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For some types of international investment funds, Cayman has become a familiar option.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A fund established there can provide a common legal structure for investors from different countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But those investors don't all stop being taxpayers in their home countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They don't automatically gain immunity from financial regulation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And they don't escape investment risk merely because the fund is offshore.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund remains exposed to the performance of its investments.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A bad investment is still a bad investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A failed company doesn't become profitable because its shares are held through Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And a poorly managed fund doesn't become safe because it is incorporated on an island.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The real attraction lies in how the structure helps organize a cross-border investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That may sound less exciting than the idea of secret money hidden on a beach.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it's much more important.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because once we follow an investment through the system, the entire map begins to change.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Northbridge Example

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Let's build a hypothetical example.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine a pension fund called Northbridge Retirement Fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Northbridge doesn't represent a particular real pension institution. We're using it to follow the mechanics of an international investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It manages retirement savings for thousands of workers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some are approaching retirement.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Others have decades of work ahead of them.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund's job is to invest money under its legal obligations and investment policies so it can help meet future pension payments.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now suppose Northbridge decides to allocate part of its portfolio to an international investment fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund's managers specialize in buying stakes in businesses across several countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They might invest in technology, manufacturing, healthcare, infrastructure, or other industries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The managers work in New York.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Several investors are in North America and Europe.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The businesses being acquired operate in different parts of the world.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the investment fund itself is established in the Cayman Islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now let's follow the relationship.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Northbridge decides to commit capital.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It reviews the relevant legal documents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It examines the investment strategy, fees, risks, reporting, and withdrawal or distribution terms.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Assuming it is authorized to participate and meets the fund's requirements, it subscribes for an interest.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That interest gives Northbridge certain rights under the fund documents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The manager is then responsible for carrying out the fund's investment strategy within the agreed mandate.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund may buy securities or invest directly in private businesses.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Payments can move through banks, custodians, brokers, and settlement arrangements in different jurisdictions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The underlying assets may be nowhere near Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the investment professionals making the decisions may work thousands of miles away.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: So what is Cayman doing?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It's the legal domicile of the fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund exists under Cayman's legal framework.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That framework helps define important rights, obligations, governance arrangements, and regulatory requirements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It does not mean every dollar subscribed to the fund must sit in a bank account on Grand Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it doesn't mean the Cayman government owns the investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Suppose the fund invests in a manufacturing company in Germany.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Northbridge's economic exposure is now connected, through the fund, to a business operating in Germany.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The investment manager may still be working in New York.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund remains legally established in Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the original retirement savings came from workers whose pension fund is based in North America.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Four very different places.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One international investment relationship.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now imagine the German company grows.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its sales increase.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its value rises.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Eventually, the fund sells its investment at a profit.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The proceeds are handled according to the fund's agreements and financial arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: After applicable costs, fees, and other obligations, the fund may distribute money to investors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Northbridge receives the amount to which it is entitled.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That money can help support its investment portfolio and future pension obligations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Where did the profit come from?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Economically, it came from the performance and sale of the underlying investment, along with the terms on which that investment was made.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Where was the investment vehicle registered?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who made the investment decisions?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The manager, according to the fund's governance arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who ultimately benefited?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The investors entitled to the returns, subject to all the costs, risks, and applicable rules.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And that's why the popular idea of money simply being sent away to an island and sitting there misses so much of what is happening.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The island may be part of the legal route through which investors hold their financial interests.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It may not be where the investment's value is created.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It may not be where the investment manager works.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it may not be where the money is ultimately paid.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now consider what happens when thousands of similar structures exist.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The recorded financial relationships involving a small jurisdiction can become enormous.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Not because that jurisdiction has suddenly developed the world's largest domestic factories or consumer market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But because entities registered there connect investors and assets from many other countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is one reason cross-border financial centers can appear so large in international financial statistics.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it also raises a question.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Why the Same Places?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Why do investors keep choosing the same places?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Why not establish every fund in the country where the manager works?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The answer reveals how financial centers become powerful.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine you're starting an investment fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You have potential investors in six countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need experienced lawyers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need administrators who understand fund reporting.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need auditors familiar with the structure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need reliable rules governing the entity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And you want to avoid creating unnecessary complications when pooling investors who have different national tax obligations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One option is to design an entirely new structure in a jurisdiction your advisers rarely use.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Another is to use a jurisdiction where an established professional industry already understands the type of fund you're creating.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For many international managers, Cayman falls into that second category.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is the advantage of specialization.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Over time, thousands of funds have been established there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Law firms have developed expertise in relevant company and fund laws.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Administrators and other service providers have become familiar with the procedures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: International managers understand the types of structures available.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Investors and their advisers may already know how to evaluate them.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That familiarity can reduce uncertainty and make a particular structure easier to organize.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There's another reason that familiarity matters.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine you're managing a pension fund worth billions of dollars.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Someone approaches you with an investment opportunity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The projected returns look attractive. The manager has experience. The strategy makes sense.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But there's a problem.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund is registered in a jurisdiction your institution has never worked with.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your legal team now has to examine an unfamiliar corporate structure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your compliance team needs to understand the regulations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your operations team needs to check whether the fund's systems and service providers meet your requirements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the investment committee wants to know what protections exist if something goes wrong.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: All of that takes time.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It may cost money.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it creates additional work before the investment can even be approved.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now imagine the same manager offers a structure your institution already understands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your legal advisers have reviewed similar funds.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Your operations team knows the reporting arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the structure has an established record of use by other institutional investors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't mean the investment is automatically safe.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The manager can still make terrible decisions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund can still lose money.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the institution has fewer unfamiliar legal and operational questions to resolve.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And for a large investor, that can make a difference.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is how an established financial center gains an advantage that isn't written on a tax-rate chart.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its reputation, professional network, and familiar legal structures can become reasons to keep using it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And those advantages can reinforce one another as more businesses enter the industry.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Tax Question

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There is also the tax treatment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman generally does not impose direct income taxes on investment funds in the way many other jurisdictions impose taxes on domestic corporations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For certain investment structures, this helps avoid adding a separate local layer of income taxation at the fund level.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it is essential to understand what that does and does not mean.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It doesn't make the investors automatically tax-free.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An investor may still owe tax under the laws of their own country.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The underlying investment can also generate taxes where business activity takes place.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Different investment types and ownership structures can produce different tax consequences.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And tax authorities may apply rules specifically designed to prevent abusive arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: So when someone describes Cayman as a tax-neutral fund jurisdiction, they are referring to a particular feature of the structure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They are not proving that nobody pays taxes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For legitimate international investment funds, avoiding an additional layer of local income taxation at the pooling vehicle can be commercially useful.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But legal familiarity, professional services, investor requirements, and regulatory obligations also influence the decision.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And something else happens when one jurisdiction becomes widely used.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It creates its own momentum.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A new manager asks a lawyer where to establish a fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The lawyer explains the available options.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One option has an extensive history with similar funds.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Administrators already support it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Investors recognize it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The manager chooses that structure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Then another manager makes a similar decision.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And another.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Over time, the jurisdiction becomes part of the industry's normal operating habits.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This doesn't mean every fund belongs there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There are significant alternatives, including European fund domiciles and domestic fund structures in major financial markets.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And some investors cannot or will not participate in particular offshore arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the accumulated experience of a financial center becomes a competitive advantage.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The result is visible in Cayman's fund statistics.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: By the third quarter of 2026, the regulator recorded 13,187 mutual funds and 18,360 private funds.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Together, 31,547 regulated funds.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now be careful with that number.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It is a count of fund structures under the regulator's published categories.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It is not a count of wealthy individuals.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It is not a count of banks.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it doesn't mean each fund has a separate office full of employees in George Town.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some structures involve extensive international networks of service providers and investment entities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What the number demonstrates is the scale of the legal and financial industry associated with the jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman became a place international investment managers knew how to use.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And once an industry becomes this established, changing its location can involve far more than moving a bank account.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Existing agreements, investor rights, taxes, regulations, service providers, and reporting requirements may all need to be reviewed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That helps explain why the business has persisted.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But so far, we've only followed the investors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We haven't asked the question that matters most to the people living on those islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who actually gets rich?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: When you see a number like sixty trillion dollars associated with international financial centers, it can create a misleading picture.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You might imagine that everyone living in those jurisdictions must be extraordinarily wealthy.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the value of international financial positions is not the same as the wealth owned by residents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A fund registered in Cayman may own investments on behalf of people living in other countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Those investors generally retain the economic rights attached to their fund interests.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Cayman government doesn't simply collect the value of the investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the local population doesn't automatically receive the fund's profits.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the financial industry does create economic activity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Think about what it takes to operate thousands of investment structures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Someone has to prepare the legal documents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Someone has to manage regulatory filings.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Funds need accountants, administrators, auditors, directors, and other professionals.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Businesses need offices.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Workers need housing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Government agencies supervise and administer parts of the system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial companies pay applicable fees.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Professional firms employ people.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the employees and businesses connected to the industry spend money within the local economy.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That creates jobs, incomes, and government revenue.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman's financial-services sector became a major part of its economic development.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the benefits aren't necessarily distributed equally.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Different workers earn different incomes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some jobs require specialized qualifications.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A growing international business sector can also place pressure on housing, infrastructure, and the cost of living.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The money flowing through a jurisdiction and the living standards of its residents are two different subjects.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Both matter.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And specialization creates risks of its own.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine a small economy whose employment, professional-services industry, and public finances depend significantly on international financial business.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What happens if global rules change?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What happens if competing jurisdictions become more attractive?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Or if a serious regulatory failure damages confidence in the territory?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The effects could reach far beyond the law firms and investment companies directly involved.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The same industry that supports growth can expose a small economy to changes made overseas.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A major government in Europe changes its tax rules.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An international financial organization tightens reporting requirements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Large institutional investors adopt new policies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And a small Caribbean territory may have to adapt.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That is one of the strange features of globalization.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An island can build a successful industry around international capital.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But its future can depend on decisions made in cities thousands of miles away.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If you're finding this useful, a like or a share helps this kind of documentary reach people who may never have come across the subject. Because offshore finance is often discussed as though it involves nothing more than wealthy people hiding cash, when the actual system is both more complicated and more important.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Wider Network

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And we've only looked at one set of islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman belongs to a much wider network.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Pull back from the Caribbean.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now look across the Atlantic.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Bermuda sits in the North Atlantic Ocean.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The British Virgin Islands lie farther south in the Caribbean region.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Jersey and Guernsey are near the coast of France.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Luxembourg is a small country surrounded by much larger European neighbors.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Ireland sits on the western edge of Europe.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And financial activity also passes through major global centers such as London, New York, Hong Kong, and Singapore.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These places play different roles.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But all are connected to international finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Bermuda has developed important insurance and reinsurance businesses.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman is particularly prominent in investment fund structures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The British Virgin Islands became known for international corporate services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Luxembourg and Ireland are major investment fund domiciles within European regulatory frameworks.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Jersey and Guernsey have their own traditions of trusts, funds, and financial services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They are not interchangeable.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Their laws differ.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Their tax systems differ.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Their regulatory obligations differ.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And they do not all serve the same clients or financial activities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But they demonstrate something that is easy to miss when we think about global finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The locations where investment decisions are made are not necessarily the same places where financial claims are legally recorded.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Suppose an international fund is established in one jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its manager operates from another.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It owns shares in companies from several countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the investors themselves live in still more locations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal connections may be recorded across several borders.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This can make a small financial jurisdiction appear very prominent in the data.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And researchers have spent years trying to understand how these structures affect measurements of the global financial system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Bank for International Settlements made this especially clear in its March 2026 research.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The study described cross-border financial centers as places that often act as intermediaries between the original source of capital and its final investment destination.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They may host entities with limited physical operations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And their international financial business can be enormous compared with their domestic economies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: From 1980 to 2023, the share of worldwide external financial positions associated with these centers increased from around twelve percent to nearly thirty percent.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That's a significant shift.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But what exactly is an external financial position?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Consider a bank in one country holding a financial claim on an entity resident in another.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Or an investor holding securities issued abroad.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: International financial statistics record different categories of cross-border assets and liabilities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These are positions measured at a point in time.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They are not simply amounts transferred during the year.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This distinction is crucial.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If someone says a country has a trillion dollars in external financial assets, they are not necessarily saying that a trillion dollars entered the country that morning, that month, or even that year.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They're describing recorded financial holdings or claims under a particular statistical definition.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now add intermediate entities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An investor in Country A wants exposure to assets in Country C.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The investment is organized through an entity in Country B.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal and financial records may show relationships involving Country B, even though the underlying investment ultimately concerns Country C.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't mean the statistics are wrong.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It means the recorded relationships need to be interpreted carefully.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If you want to know who ultimately owns an asset, you may need to look past the immediate intermediary.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If you want to know where the economic risk lies, you may need to examine the underlying investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And if you want to understand how financial distress could spread between countries, you may need to know more than the address on the company documents.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is one of the reasons international finance can be difficult to understand.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We often see the final numbers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But we don't see the chain of relationships beneath them.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And one recent report shows just how strange that financial map can look.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The U.S. Treasury Data

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In November 2026, the United States Treasury published detailed figures showing where American investors held foreign securities at the end of 2025.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You might expect the largest destination to be Britain.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Or Japan.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Perhaps Canada, one of America's largest trading partners.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the jurisdiction at the top of that particular list wasn't any of them.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It was the Cayman Islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: American investors held approximately 3.07 trillion dollars in foreign securities attributed to Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: More than the 2 trillion attributed to the United Kingdom.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: More than the 1.88 trillion attributed to Canada.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And more than twice the amount attributed to Japan.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now think about that for a moment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: We're talking about three small Caribbean islands appearing above some of the world's largest economies in an official American investment survey.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman didn't suddenly become a bigger industrial economy than Japan.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And Americans didn't physically ship three trillion dollars to its beaches.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The figures measure the market value of foreign securities held by U.S. investors and attributed to particular jurisdictions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A large part of the Cayman figure reflects the territory's role in international investment structures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And that is precisely why this matters.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine an American investment institution purchasing a security issued by a fund legally established in Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund may hold assets connected to businesses operating elsewhere.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the security owned by the American investor is associated with the Cayman entity.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: So Cayman can appear in the statistics even when the underlying economic activity takes place in another country.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal route of the investment changes how the financial relationship appears on the map.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't make the investment fictional.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The investor still owns a real financial claim, with real risks and potential returns.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it means the country shown in the statistics may not tell you where the ultimate business activity happens.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And here's what makes the figure so revealing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These numbers come from the United States Treasury itself.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You don't need a leaked document or a hidden bank record to see the scale of the relationship.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It's sitting in official financial statistics.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The harder question is understanding what those statistics actually represent.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because Cayman being at the top of this list doesn't mean the islands are the final destination of America's foreign investment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It shows how deeply these financial structures have become embedded in the way international investments are organized.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: When people talk about money moving around the world, the financial map they imagine may be very different from the map recorded in the official numbers.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial centers can influence how international financial integration appears in the data.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And researchers have to work carefully to distinguish the immediate location of a claim from the ultimate investor or final economic exposure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial Secrecy

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Which brings us to another question.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If so much of this system is legitimate, why has offshore finance developed such a troubling reputation?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The answer begins with the difference between financial privacy and financial secrecy.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine a person owns a company.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That company owns another company.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The second company owns a third.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the third holds a financial asset.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There may be valid commercial reasons for some of those arrangements.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Different businesses may need separate legal entities to manage liabilities, ownership interests, or particular activities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the structure creates a question.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Who ultimately controls the asset?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Knowing the name of the company written on the document may not be enough.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Authorities may need to identify the people who ultimately own or control the legal entities.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is known as beneficial ownership.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the distinction becomes important when investigators are trying to determine whether financial activity is lawful.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Suppose a company receives payments connected to a criminal investigation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An authority may want to identify the people controlling the company.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the registered shareholder is another company.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That company is owned by an entity in another jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And part of the ownership chain involves arrangements that require additional legal investigation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Each extra layer may make the work more demanding.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The structure may be legitimate.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But if information is missing, inaccurate, or difficult for authorities to obtain, the system becomes vulnerable to misuse.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial secrecy can help conceal corruption.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It can make tax evasion harder to detect.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It can be used in money laundering.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it can obstruct efforts to identify the people behind suspicious transactions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But we also need to separate several activities that are often confused.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Tax planning is not automatically tax evasion.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: International investment is not automatically money laundering.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And an offshore fund is not automatically a secret account.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Tax evasion involves illegal noncompliance with tax obligations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Money laundering involves handling criminal proceeds in ways intended to disguise or otherwise deal with their illicit origin.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Lawful tax planning involves arranging affairs within applicable rules, although some aggressive arrangements may be challenged under anti-avoidance laws.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These are different things.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the existence of one does not prove the existence of another.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An international pension fund may use an offshore investment vehicle for legitimate reasons.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A criminal may also try to exploit offshore structures to conceal assets.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal form alone doesn't tell you which situation you're looking at.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need facts.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need ownership information.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You need transaction records.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And you need authorities capable of enforcing the law.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is where international cooperation becomes essential.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Money and financial relationships cross borders.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But investigators usually operate under the legal authority of particular countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They often need information from other jurisdictions to complete their work.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That requires rules for sharing information.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It requires effective regulators.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it requires records that can actually be obtained when needed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Over time, countries have introduced stronger standards for anti-money-laundering controls, tax information exchange, and beneficial ownership reporting.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Financial Action Task Force has played an important role in establishing global standards against money laundering and terrorist financing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: International tax cooperation has also expanded through the OECD and the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial account reporting has become more extensive.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Beneficial ownership requirements have developed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And offshore jurisdictions have faced increasing pressure to meet international expectations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But passing a law and making that law work are not always the same thing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And Cayman's regulatory history shows why.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Regulation & Reform

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In 2021, the Financial Action Task Force placed the Cayman Islands under increased monitoring.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That meant the jurisdiction had identified strategic deficiencies to address under an agreed action plan.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It did not mean every financial business in Cayman was engaged in wrongdoing.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it did not mean every investor using Cayman was doing something illegal.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It meant the jurisdiction's framework for preventing and addressing financial crime needed improvements in particular areas.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Cayman undertook reforms.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In October 2023, FATF announced that the Cayman Islands would no longer be subject to its increased monitoring process.

visual.title: FATF
visual.sub: Cayman Islands removed from increased monitoring — October 2023

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The decision followed an assessment of the progress made in addressing the identified deficiencies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That was a significant development for the jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its financial industry depends heavily on maintaining confidence among international clients and counterparties.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Regulatory reputation matters.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If banks, investors, and financial institutions lose confidence in a jurisdiction's compliance systems, the commercial consequences can be serious.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But removal from increased monitoring did not mean that every transparency issue had disappeared.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In June 2026, the OECD published an updated report examining Cayman's implementation of standards for exchanging tax information upon request.

visual.title: OECD REVIEW
visual.sub: Tax Information Exchange — Cayman Islands, June 2026

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The findings were mixed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The report acknowledged changes to Cayman's beneficial ownership framework and other efforts.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it also identified recommendations that had not yet been fully addressed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Among the concerns were effective oversight of accounting record requirements and the ability to obtain information held outside the territory.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The report also raised concerns about the timeliness of responses to international information requests.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: For the monitored period covering 2023 and 2024, Cayman reported that only 23 percent of incoming requests received responses within ninety days.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The report documented progress in some areas while calling for further action in others.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is important because it shows how financial regulation works in the real world.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A jurisdiction can strengthen its rules and still face practical problems.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An international organization can recognize significant improvements while another review identifies remaining weaknesses.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And none of that can be reduced to a simple claim that the entire system is either safe or corrupt.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The real question is whether the rules are effective.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Can authorities identify beneficial owners?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Can they obtain accurate financial records?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Can they respond to requests from other countries?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Can they investigate violations?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And are the consequences serious enough to encourage compliance?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: These questions apply far beyond the Cayman Islands.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Large financial centers face problems involving financial crime, ownership structures, and international transactions too.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Money laundering does not become less serious because it passes through a major European capital instead of a Caribbean jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the history and business models of certain offshore centers have made them a particular focus of international scrutiny.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And the most politically sensitive part of that scrutiny concerns taxation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Because when money crosses borders, governments want to know where profits should be taxed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Consider two companies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One earns money by selling products in a large domestic market.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It has employees, factories, offices, and customers there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The other is an investment vehicle legally registered in a different jurisdiction.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It holds assets for investors based in several countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Both may be involved in international finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But their economic activities are not the same.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And their tax treatment may be very different.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This distinction matters because public debates often place investment funds, multinational companies, holding companies, banks, and private wealth arrangements into one category called offshore money.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: In reality, they serve different purposes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A multinational company may use subsidiaries in different countries to conduct business, own intellectual property, borrow money, or hold investments.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A fund may be created to pool money from investors and acquire assets.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A trust may be used to hold or manage property under particular legal obligations.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The tax questions depend on the structure and the relevant laws.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: One important debate concerns multinational companies reporting profits in jurisdictions where relatively little underlying economic activity takes place.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Governments want to know whether profits are being allocated in a way that reflects the actual business.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They also want to protect the tax revenue used to fund public services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Businesses, meanwhile, want predictable rules for transactions that involve more than one country.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And investors want to avoid unnecessary complexity and double taxation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Different governments have different tax systems.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some rely heavily on corporate and personal income taxes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Others collect more revenue through consumption taxes, property charges, customs duties, or other sources.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The Cayman Islands is unusual because it has no ordinary direct income tax system of the type used by many large economies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its government instead relies on revenue sources that include duties, fees, and other charges.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That can make Cayman attractive for certain international structures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the absence of Cayman income tax doesn't erase taxation everywhere else.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Suppose a company operates in Germany and earns taxable profits there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Putting its shares inside a Cayman fund does not automatically remove every German tax obligation.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Likewise, an investor living in another country may still have reporting and tax obligations under that country's laws.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The result depends on the circumstances.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And tax authorities may challenge arrangements they consider abusive or inconsistent with the law.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A major concern in international taxation is the movement of profits between related companies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A multinational group may have subsidiaries in different countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It may conduct transactions between those subsidiaries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And governments need rules to determine how much income belongs to each jurisdiction for tax purposes.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is different from a pension fund investing through a foreign-domiciled vehicle.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Both involve cross-border finance.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But they are not the same financial mechanism.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The distinction is more than a technical detail.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If we treat every offshore structure as though it operates in exactly the same way, we lose the ability to identify where the real problems are.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some arrangements exist to pool international investment efficiently.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some exist to manage legal and commercial risks.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some are motivated partly by tax treatment.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And some are designed or used in ways that violate the law.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The challenge for governments is to distinguish them and enforce the rules fairly.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That challenge has become more difficult as global financial relationships have grown.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A company can sell products in dozens of countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A fund can hold assets around the world.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: An investment manager can serve clients who have never visited the jurisdiction where the fund is registered.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And financial returns may pass through several entities before reaching their final owner.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The world economy is connected.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But governments still collect taxes through legal systems largely organized around national territory.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That tension is one reason the offshore finance debate has continued for decades.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it leads to a difficult question.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Could It Be Stopped?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Could the world simply stop using small offshore financial centers?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Suppose a group of major economies decided that investment funds should no longer use Cayman.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: What would happen?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some funds might move to other jurisdictions.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some managers might reorganize their structures.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Certain activities might become more expensive.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some investors could face different regulatory or tax consequences.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And some financial business could shift to places already offering competing services.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the underlying need to organize international investments would not disappear.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Investors would still live in different countries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Businesses would still need capital.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Pension funds would still seek diversified investments.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial managers would still need legal structures through which clients could own assets.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And national legal systems would still differ.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't mean every existing offshore structure is necessary.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It doesn't mean the current distribution of financial business is ideal.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it doesn't mean governments should accept harmful practices simply because international investment is complicated.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It means the demand for cross-border legal and financial arrangements is real.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Removing one jurisdiction from the system would not automatically remove that demand.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It could instead move the business somewhere else.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And that is what makes competition between financial centers so interesting.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A small jurisdiction can attract international business by offering legal structures and professional services that investors find useful.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But it has to remain competitive.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If other jurisdictions develop better structures, lower costs, or more attractive regulations, business can shift.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If the rules become too burdensome, some clients may look elsewhere.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: If oversight is too weak, the jurisdiction can face reputational and commercial damage.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And if major investors decide they no longer want to use a particular location, the jurisdiction cannot simply force them to stay.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This is why offshore financial centers are not guaranteed permanent success.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Their advantages depend on international confidence.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A jurisdiction needs to be attractive to legitimate businesses while maintaining standards that enable it to participate in the global financial system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That balance is difficult.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it becomes even more complicated when international tax and regulatory rules change.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some structures that were attractive twenty years ago may offer fewer advantages today.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Other structures may remain useful because of their legal design, professional expertise, or established market practices.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The financial map can change.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And history tells us that centers of financial power do not stay in the same places forever.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Venice was once an important center of international commerce.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Amsterdam became a major financial hub during the rise of Dutch trade.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: London expanded its global financial influence over centuries.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: New York developed into one of the world's dominant capital markets.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The reasons behind those transformations differed.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But they reveal a common pattern.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Financial importance depends on institutions, relationships, access to capital, commercial activity, and the confidence of the people using the system.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It isn't simply determined by how much land a country controls.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Or how many people live there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Which brings us back to the tiny islands that started this story.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Their importance comes from a particular part of the international financial network.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Not from possessing the world's largest domestic economies.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And not from owning all the money associated with the financial entities registered there.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: They became important because global investors repeatedly chose to use their legal and professional infrastructure.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: There's one more part of the story worth understanding.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And it concerns the way we measure financial risk.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Imagine an investor in Country A buying an asset in Country C through a fund in Country B.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The fund is the immediate legal vehicle.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the underlying business operates in Country C.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Now suppose the business encounters financial trouble.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its revenue falls.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Its borrowing costs rise.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: And its value declines.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The investor in Country A may suffer losses through the fund.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The legal structure in Country B remains part of the chain.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But the underlying economic problem began elsewhere.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: This matters when analysts study financial exposure across borders.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: A financial position recorded against an entity in one jurisdiction may ultimately be connected to risks in another.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Different statistical methods can help identify these relationships.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: But interpreting them requires care.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: You can't always understand who faces the final economic risk simply by looking at the immediate country associated with a financial claim.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: That doesn't mean every international fund is dangerously complicated.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: It means financial relationships can involve layers that matter when something goes wrong.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Some structures are straightforward.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Others are highly complex.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
